newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trelleborg sells Boliden at C$16/share.
newsitem.headline: Trelleborg sells Boliden at C$16/share.

text.p: Swedish mining and rubber group Trelleborg said on Wednesday it was selling its Boliden metals and mining unit for C$16 a share.
Boliden said in a statement that it would sell 51 million Boliden shares with a total value of C$813 million which would represent about 56.1 percent of the unit.
Boliden will be listed on the Toronto and Montreal stock exchanges on June 17.
A group of investment banks lead by Nesbitt Burns will buy the shares, the company said.
Payment has been divided into two with the first instalment of C$8 a share due on June 17 this year and the second of C$8 a share on June 17 next year.
"On top of that the investment banks will have options on an overallotment," the company said.
Trelleborg said if the banks use their options in full, the market will hold 56.1 percent of Boliden.
"The reception of Boliden's introduction has been fantastic both in Europe and North America," Trelleborg chief executive Kjell Nilsson said in the statement.
"That the company is valued at nine billion crowns is well in line with our highest expectations."

But dealers said the price was lower than expected and Trelleborg's share dropped on the news, trading 2.5 crowns lower at 131 crowns at 1030 GMT while the Stockholm Stock Exchange's general index was up 0.01 percent at 2,888.46.
Trelleborg announced on May 2 it was seeking a listing for Boliden in Canada, saying it would retain between 45 percent and 49 percent of the group.
